newsitem.title: EGYPT: Israel submits new Hebron plan, Arafat angry.
newsitem.headline: Israel submits new Hebron plan, Arafat angry.

text.p: Israel gave the Palestinians a new plan for redeployment in the town of Hebron on Tuesday night and Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat said angrily on Wednesday he had complained about it to Egypt and the European Union.
He said the plan divided the West Bank town in two parts and gave Israel the right of hot pursuit into the Palestinian part.
Arafat described the Israeli plan as a tragedy. "It's a dangerous operation. It shows Israel's aggressive intentions in Hebron and shows complete and abhorrent racism," he added.

"There's no doubt this plan will cause an outcry not just among Palestinians. It will cause an outcry among Palestinians, in the Arab world and internationally," said Arafat, who waved the document in the air at the presidential palace in Cairo.
Asked about the latest round of talks with Israel on Hebron, he said: "It's passing through very, very difficult circumstances and the impact is very dangerous."
Arafat said he had shown the document to the ambassadors of Ireland, the Netherlands and Italy, the current, former and future presidents of the European Union.
